preconditions.description: The input integer n (number of vertices) is within the range [2, 300000].

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= u < v <= n for u, v, _ in edges) and len(edges) == n - 1
preconditions.description: The broom is a valid tree with n vertices, where edges are directed from parent u to child v, and there are exactly n-1 edges. Vertex 1 is the root.

preconditions.expression: all(isinstance(x, str) and len(x) == 1 and x.islower() for _, _, x in edges)
preconditions.description: Each edge is labeled with a single lowercase Latin letter.
The edges are parsed from the input lines after the first line (n). Each edge line is split into u, v, and x.

postconditions.description: The output consists of exactly two lines: the first line is the minimum possible size of the broom after simplification, and the second line is the integer p.

postconditions.expression: min_size == min(broom_size(p) for p in range(1, max_word_length + 1) if p <= max_word_length) and p == min({p for p in range(1, max_word_length + 1) if broom_size(p) == min_size})
postconditions.description: The output p is the smallest integer such that the broom size after simplification with p is minimized. The first line of output is the minimum broom size achievable by any valid p.

postconditions.expression: max_word_length >= 1 and all(len(word) >= 1 for word in words)
postconditions.description: The words in the language (derived from the broom) have lengths >= 1, and max_word_length is the maximum word length in the language.
The broom size after simplification with p is computed correctly, and p is a valid simplification position (1 ≤ p ≤ max_word_length).
The broom size after simplification is always between 1 (root) and n (original size).
